rules: Crossover proposals multiplying or adding the ROA rank with an unrelated price-based rank term keep failing the fusion check for sharing only 2 nodes; avoid shallow top-level fusions with ROA this round.

Rank or argmax transforms applied directly to raw volume or dollar volume, with no normalization, failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.46 to 0.74); use volume/dollar volume as a normalizer inside a feature, not as the ranked quantity itself.
Correlating volume (or sign of return) with returns over 21 to 63 day windows produced the weakest scores of the round (|t| 0.02 to 0.36); deprioritize volume-return correlation as a feature family.

A 252-day window on volume or dollar volume dropped coverage to exactly 0.874 in both instances this round, just under the 0.90 floor, while 63-day windows on the same fields passed coverage fine; avoid 252-day volume windows.

Changing only the lookback window on an already-archived expression (10 vs 21, or 63 vs 21) reliably triggers the correlation gate at rho 0.94 to 0.98; vary the functional form, not just window length, when building on archived structures.

Raw dollar volume and its medium-window mean both duplicate the archived short-window dollar-volume mean at rho above 0.93; this normalizer is saturated, so pair dollar volume with a new signal rather than proposing it alone.

All three accepts this round pair a price range (high-low or high-close distance) with a dollar-volume or liquidity-rank normalizer, spanning fast, medium, and slow speed niches; this structure is currently the productive one, favor it over fundamentals crossovers.

A near-duplicate of the round's top accepted factor, differing by one normalizer swap, was rejected for sharing 5 nodes with it; edits to a freshly-accepted winner need a different normalizer or range definition, not a single-node swap, to count as novel.
